div.p: Having built enough conceptual scaffolding at the end of the previous chapter to address the Cornell 7 case in all its depth, we now turn our gaze toward the wider picture of Western cultural evolution over the last two centuries.

div.head: 10.1 Three Stages of Girardian Decay
div.p: As René Girard traces in Deceit, Desire, and the Novel, the erosion of Christian vertical transcendence and the dismantling of the internalized Kullaba (porneiomachia) do not liberate the modern subject into autonomous, Rousseauian freedom; instead, they trigger a progressive, three-stage pathology of metaphysical desire. In the first stage, as the Western elite began abandoning orthodox Christian faith, it initially attempted to stave off the resulting ontological void without overtly regressing to the brute force of the archaic E-Anna warlord. Exploiting the secular entertainment loophole first engineered by the medieval troubadours (Section 8.2.4) alongside the intellectualized Sofia Neoplatonic cult pioneered at the court of Frederick II (Section 8.3.3) and prepared philosophically by Duns Scotus’s univocatio entis, Western modernity erected a pantheon of positive, secularized idols operating in the red of external mediation. Chief among these romantique substitutes were the Sublime Artist—the solitary, tormented creative genius whose ego supposedly generates masterpieces ex nihilo like a god, as seen in our case study of Virginia Woolf (Section 3.3); the Revolutionary Redeemer, born of the French Revolution (Section 8.5.5), who promised that violently decapitating the traditional monarch would usher in a rationalist utopia of civic virtue; the Scientific Genius, the high priest of Sofia whose mathematical mastery of the material universe would deliver ontological fullness; and finally the Screen Celebrity, the direct modern descendant of courtly fiction, revered by the public from afar as an untouchable, polished demigod.

By the late twentieth century, however, the second stage—the Great Disappointment—had set in, as every single one of these positive human mediators went ontologically bankrupt. Girard’s geometry of desire explains why this collapse was inevitable: because a human model’s perceived divinity is merely a mimetic mirage projected by the subject, any positive ideal that can actually be inspected, imitated, or attained at close range immediately loses its transcendent aura as the dynamic slides from external mediation into the envious rivalry of internal mediation (the black). Across Western high culture, as artists realized that aesthetic beauty could no longer deliver metaphysical transfiguration—the exact post-publication awful blankness that haunted Woolf—they turned against beauty itself, resorting to ironic, scatological non-art and deliberately vandalizing aesthetic standards to prove their superiority over a naive public. Simultaneously, just as the rationalist utopia of 1789 instantly collapsed into Napoleonic military despotism, the twentieth century’s secular revolutions terminated in bureaucratic terror, the Gulag, and the nihilistic self-slaughter prefigured in Dostoevsky’s Demons (Section 3.4). Concurrently, the cult of the Scientific Genius stalled out: with fundamental physics largely frozen since the 1970s into untestable abstractions and academic hyper-specialization, the stalled priests of Sofia began feeling like hollow ensi clerks, explaining why elite theoretical physicists and evolutionary biologists would soon flock so eagerly to Jeffrey Epstein’s court (Section 8.3.3). Finally, ubiquitous, 24/7, social media access dissolved the protective distance shielding the Celebrity, exposing the once-heroic screen idol as neurotic, manufactured, and spiritually empty.

This universal bankruptcy of positive ideals propels Western culture directly into the third and terminal stage of Girardian decay: the masochistic inversion, i.e. the turn to demonic masters. When every benevolent, rational, or lawful model has been unmasked as a fraud—perceived as merely another anxious, powerless atom trapped inside an idolatrous prison of his own making—the modern subject’s pride (vanité) still refuses to relinquish metaphysical desire and submit to the Christian God. Instead, the subject doubles down through a perverse ontological deduction: if goodness and lawfulness are the hallmarks of weak, domesticated Kullaba clerks (as Nietzsche would have it), then the only way a mediator can prove he genuinely possesses untouchable, sovereign autonomy is by being openly evil, cruel, and above the law. As Girard diagnoses in the passages cited in Sections 3.2 and 9.10, we no longer choose our mediator for the admiration he inspires, but because of the disgust we seem to inspire in him, turning frantically toward the one who makes [us] suffer so that the executioner might prove to him that he is a god. Once Western society crosses this threshold, its unacknowledged religion (the NRM of section 1.5) sheds its polite Apollonian and humanist alibis, mutating into an explicit, sado-masochistic worship of the transgressive (toxic) BDMB—a cultural landscape where, from the highest echelons of the global ruling class down to the undergraduate fraternity house, only a cruel, boundary-shattering master can still simulate a spark of the sacred.

div.head: 10.2 The Literary Arc — From Lord Byron to the A-Man
div.p: Nowhere is this three-stage Girardian descent more transparently documented than in the evolution of Western romantic literature over the past two centuries, which bridges the gap between the medieval stealth religion of courtly love (Section 8.2) and contemporary FCNSW (Section 9.10). Whereas medieval fin'amor placed the male knight in a posture of Platonic submission before the Marian-adjacent midons, nineteenth-century Romanticism violently inverted the gender polarity of the stealth religion. As the romantique buildup of the autonomous human hero collided with the perceived sterility of bourgeois Christian morality, the idealized male mediator rapidly darkened into a monster, placing the female reader in a posture of masochistic adoration before an explicitly Luciferian BDMB. The Italian literary critic Mario Praz, in his landmark study The Romantic Agony, traced the exact philological lineage of this Metamorphosis of Satan: John Milton’s rebellious Lucifer in Paradise Lost—already celebrated by Romantic poets as the supreme insurgent against the Paternal Kullaba—was transmuted via eighteenth-century Gothic villains directly into the historical and literary persona of Lord Byron.

cit.quote: The Accursed, the Fallen Angel [see Enochian parallels in section 7.1.2], had become the Ideal of the nineteenth century... From Milton's Satan to the Gothic villain, and finally to the Byronic hero, the rebel against God and society acquires a sinister, irresistible fascination: it is precisely his crime, his cruelty, and his damnation that endow him with a superhuman, fatal majesty in the eyes of his victims.
cit.bibl: Mario Praz, The Romantic Agony, trans. Angus Davidson (London: Oxford University Press, 1933), p. 61.

div.p: When Lady Caroline Lamb famously described Byron in her journal in 1812 as mad, bad, and dangerous to know, she articulated the first modern formulation of badass worship: she did not desire Byron despite his wickedness, but because of his incestuous, aristocratic disdain for common morality—the exact ethos later institutionalized by the Bloomsbury Group and the Mountbattens (Section 2.3.2).

This Luciferian BDMB was immediately domesticated and installed at the heart of women's literature by Charlotte and Emily Brontë. Long before they created Edward Rochester in Jane Eyre and Heathcliff in Wuthering Heights, the Brontë sisters spent their adolescence in their parsonage constructing secret imaginary kingdoms (Angria and Gondal) explicitly modeled on their juvenile obsession with Lord Byron. Charlotte Brontë’s central hero in the Angria manuscripts—Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Zamorna—is a ruthless, polygamous, cruel military despot (a textbook case of Sargonitis, see section 8.2.1) whom the female characters worship with slavish, self-annihilating devotion. When Emily Brontë later unleashed Heathcliff upon English literature, she simply stripped this Byronic Satan of his aristocratic titles and presented him as raw, kinetic E-Anna violence—a man explicitly described throughout the novel as a ghoul, a fiend, and an incarnate goblin, whose freezing cruelty toward Isabella Linton only intensifies her masochistic compulsion to submit to him:

cit.quote: Tell her what Heathcliff is: an unreclaimed creature, without refinement, without cultivation; an arid wilderness of furze and whinstone... Pray, don't imagine that he conceals depths of benevolence and affection beneath a stern exterior! He's not a rough diamond—a pearl-containing oyster of a rustic: he's a fierce, pitiless, wolfish man.
cit.bibl: Emily Brontë, Wuthering Heights (London: Thomas Cautley Newby, 1847), ch. 10, p. 226.

div.p: While the nineteenth-century English novel still wrapped this FCNSW monster-worship in poetic moorland mist, the twentieth-century French literary avant-garde systematically stripped away the romantique veil to expose the raw sadomasochistic mechanics underneath. Drawing directly upon the anti-theology of the Marquis de Sade (Section 8.3.3)—whom post-war French intellectuals like Simone de Beauvoir, Georges Bataille, and Michel Foucault eagerly rehabilitated as the supreme philosopher of human liberation—the elite French literary editor Dominique Aury (writing under the pseudonym Pauline Réage) published Histoire d'O (Story of O) in 1954.Aury famously wrote Histoire d'O specifically to retain the waning desire of her older lover and mediator, Jean Paulhan, the powerful director of La Nouvelle Revue Française, who had challenged her that no woman was capable of writing genuine sadomasochistic erotica; see Régine Deforges, O m'a dit: Entretiens avec Pauline Réage (Paris: Jean-Jacques Pauvert, 1975). In Story of O, a modern Parisian woman is taken by her lover to an aristocratic château at Roissy (a literary cross between Sade’s Silling and Crowley’s Abbey of Thelema), where she is chained, whipped, sodomized, branded, and passed around a fraternity of elite men:

cit.quote: You are here to serve your masters... Your hands are not your own, nor are your breasts, nor, most especially, any of your bodily orifices, which we may explore and penetrate at our pleasure... She was no longer free? Yes! Thank God, she was no longer free... she loved the idea of torture, and when she was beneath his gaze and in his hands, she was utterly happy that he made her feel so cruelly that she belonged to him.
cit.bibl: Pauline Réage, Story of O, trans. Sabine d'Estrée (New York: Grove Press, 1965), pp. 15-17, 38.

div.p: Crucially, Réage frames O’s total physical and psychological degradation not as secular abuse, but as an ascetic, quasi-monastic state of grace—an inverted theurgy in which the annihilation of the female ego beneath the collective whip of the Männerbund delivers the ontological peace that modern freedom could not provide.

By the early twenty-first century, this exact French esoteric prototype had been thoroughly democratized, culminating in the high-brow literary memoirs of the coastal elite and the mass-market industrialization of the Fifty Shades copycat empire. The most diagnostic document of this terminal stage is the 2004 bestseller The Surrender: An Erotic Memoir by Toni Bentley, a former George Balanchine ballerina representing the pinnacle of high-art aesthetic capital. Executing the exact heterosexual counterpart to Michel Foucault’s San Francisco bathhouse limit-experiences (Section 9.7), Bentley explicitly frames her sodomitical submission to a dominant, emotionally detached lover—whom she reverently christens the A-Man—not as a mere physical preference, but as a literal religious epiphany:

cit.quote: Submission is my strength, my protection, my liberation. Through my submission I have found my voice, my power, my self—and my God... When a man takes a woman in her ass, he possesses her in a way that is absolute, beyond biology, beyond procreation, beyond the laws of nature and church. It is the ultimate transgression, and in that transgression lies the holy.
cit.bibl: Toni Bentley, The Surrender: An Erotic Memoir (New York: ReganBooks, 2004), pp. 65, 118.

div.p: Here, we may note, the contrast with the Cornell 7 police report (Section 1.1) is striking, but also revealing: whereas the nineteen-year-old undergraduate Jane Doe yells Hell No to a foursome specifically because [she] knew that a foursome meant that [she] would have to take part in anal sex—the fully indoctrinated FCNSW clerisy of high-brow publishing actively evangelizes crossing that final threshold of degradation as the supreme sacrament of spiritual transfiguration. Is the last-minute opt out of Jane Doe a vestigial Kullaba restraint or the reservation of her backdoor virginity for a future A Man? We may know one day perhaps, when Jane Doe writes her memoirs.

In the wake of Réage, Bentley, and the 165-million-copy explosion of Fifty Shades of Grey, contemporary women’s literature has mutated into a multi-billion-dollar global industry of Dark Romance copycats—books churning out endless variations of billionaire sadists, mafia executioners, and literal, horned demons who stalk, abduct, and sodomize the heroine into ontological bliss. Stripped of all romantique pretense, the post-Christian literary arc leaves the FCNSW female reader metaphorically—and, in the ritual praxis of Bentley and the McThelema frat house, quite literally—on all fours with her behind up in the air, waiting to be transfixed by the sacred linga of the toxic MCNSW male. Our invocation of the Indian linga here is not a mere rhetorical flourish; it is an exact structural homology. As we established in Section 5.4.7 (and footnote 22, citing Wendy Doniger O'Flaherty), the mature Hindu synthesis stabilized the destructive, transgressive E-Anna drift of the Second Function warband (Indra/Rudra) into the worship of Shiva’s erect phallus—the linga—paired with the fierce, martial-erotic energy of the goddess (shakti). However, whereas classical India contained this phallic worship within the strict, external orthopraxic boundaries of the Brahmin Kullaba, the postmodern West—having demolished its Christian porneiomachia—has regressed to an unmediated, savage linga cult in the black, where the Sadean BDMB phallus is worshipped as the sole remaining axis of the cosmos.

What is perhaps most chilling about this two-hundred-year literary trajectory is that it was diagnosed, unmasked, and prophetically warned against long before it reached its current industrial scale—and yet those warnings had zero effect. Already in 1872, in Demons (Section 3.4), Fyodor Dostoevsky consciously constructed the character of Nikolai Stavrogin as a ruthless romanesque deconstruction of the romantique Byronic hero. Dostoevsky stripped away the Brontëan poetic glamour to reveal what the worshipped badass idol actually is: an ontologically empty monster who seduces women across all social classes, violates a child, and leaves a wake of suicides and murders precisely because his followers project their own starved desire for divinity onto his freezing, sadistic indifference. Nearly a century later, in 1961, René Girard published Deceit, Desire, and the Novel, laying bare the exact mathematical geometry of this masochistic inversion and demonstrating how the death of Christian vertical transcendence inevitably enslaves the modern subject to an executioner. And yet, despite Dostoevsky’s prophetic masterpiece and Girard’s clinical autopsy, absolutely nothing happened. The cultural juggernaut did not pause; the warning was ignored by an intelligentsia already addicted to its own disease, and the Western stampede toward monster-worship continued unabated.

div.head: 10.3 The Guru-Hero Arc — From Peace and Love to Epstein and NXIVM
div.p: In strict parallel with the literary mutation of the romantique hero, the countercultural quest for spiritual enlightenment outside Christianity followed the exact same three-stage Girardian descent, moving rapidly from the ridiculous to the tragic. In the 1950s and early 1960s, as the Beat Generation (Section 2.4) gave way to the Hippie movement, Stage 1 manifested as a naive, superficial fascination with Eastern mysticism, Peace and Love, and the benevolent Guru. As Jack Kerouac’s romanticized invocations of Tibetan yab-yum popularized the notion that easternized sexual rituals could gently dissolve the bourgeois ego, thousands of Western youths flocked to ashrams and California communes seeking a benevolent, Apollonian guide to cosmic consciousness. Yet, because these self-appointed gurus operated entirely outside the regulatory checks of either a traditional Asian Brahmin Kullaba or the Christian porneiomachia, the Peace and Love mirage collapsed almost instantaneously into Stage 2 cynicism and Stage 3 predation-masochism. By 1969, the trajectory had already produced its first demonic prototype on the fringes of the Los Angeles music elite: Charles Manson, who weaponized psychedelic drugs, pseudo-Eastern mumbo-jumbo, and mandatory group-sex rituals to forge a murderous, gender-inverted thiasus of young women willing to slaughter on his command.

By the turn of the twenty-first century, this countercultural guru apparatus had shed its tie-dye rags, migrated into the upper echelons of corporate and technocratic power, and bifurcated along class lines into two structurally identical, sadomasochistic E-Anna cults: Jeffrey Epstein’s network at the absolute apex of the global ruling class, and Keith Raniere’s NXIVM organization among the upper-middle-class and Hollywood strivers. In effect, Epstein was the elite’s Raniere, and Raniere was the poor man’s (or rather, the mid-tier heiress’s) Epstein. When placed side by side, the institutional homology between the two operations is so exact that it exposes the underlying mechanical blueprint of the postmodern E-Anna:

list.item: The Sofia Bait (Intellectual Gnosis): Neither man presented himself merely as a libertine; both masqueraded as high priests of Sofia. Raniere—whom his followers reverently addressed as Vanguard—claimed to possess one of the highest IQs in history and marketed Executive Success Programs based on patented, pseudo-mathematical rationalism. Epstein styled himself as a billionaire science philanthropist and transhumanist visionary, surrounding himself with Nobel laureate physicists, evolutionary biologists, and AI pioneers.

The Harem of Inanna priestesses: Beneath this Sofia veneer, the core operational engine of both cults was a walled-off, sacer sexual harem—Epstein’s private Caribbean island (Little Saint James) and Manhattan townhouse, and Raniere’s secluded suburban compound in Clifton Park, New York—where young women were systematically groomed to service the BDMB and his inner circle.

The Procurer-Priestess Twins (Ghislaine Maxwell and Nancy Salzman): Crucially, neither BDMB could recruit his female sacrifices alone; both relied on an older, socially respectable, high-status female lieutenant to disarm and induct the victims. Epstein deployed Ghislaine Maxwell, the British aristocrat who provided old-world social polish and recruited vulnerable girls under the guise of mentorship, while Raniere deployed Nancy Salzman, whom the cult titled Prefect, a former psychiatric nurse and hypnotist who lent therapeutic credibility to the operation, assisted by a secondary tier of Hollywood actresses like Allison Mack.

The Blackmail Egregore and Masochistic Branding: Both systems seem to have forged an unbreakable, covert egregore in the black through kompromat (blackmail collateral). In the case of Epstein it appears that the loyalty of certain global statesmen and titans of industry was strengthened by involving them in illicit sexual transgressions inside properties wired with hidden cameras. In Raniere's case, the operation of his inner master-slave sorority DOS (Dominus Obsequious Sororium) has been documented in judicial proceedings. It required female initiates to hand over nude photographs and damning personal confessions as collateral, before subjecting them to a literal Story of O ritual in which they were held down naked and cauterized near their groin with a branding iron bearing Raniere’s initials:

cit.quote: Before she was branded, Sarah had to say: Master, please brand me, it would be an honor. She was told that this was not a mark of victimhood, but a mark of ultimate strength—that by submitting her body to pain and permanent ownership, she was transcending her fears and becoming a sovereign woman.
cit.bibl: Sarah Edmondson, Scarred: The True Story of How I Escaped NXIVM, the Cult That Bound My Life (New York: Chronicle Prism, 2019), p. 184.

div.p: As we briefly noted in Section 8.3.3, both Epstein and Raniere were unconsciously executing the exact medieval blueprint of Frederick II Hohenstaufen at Palermo: the fusion of Sofia with Inanna. Why did this specific combination prove so irresistible to the postmodern Western elite? Because in the contemporary Liberal State (Section 9.5), the official, public avenues to power—academia, corporate finance, international politics—are locked inside Max Weber’s rationalized iron cage. A theoretical physicist at Harvard, a tech billionaire, or a Western Prime Minister possesses immense institutional authority, yet within the public square they must constantly perform the castrated, egalitarian pieties of the secularized Kullaba. Thermodynamically, they feel like frauds—mere ensi clerks deprived of the visceral, untouchable sovereignty of the ancient lugal. Epstein solved their ontological starvation by uniting the two halves of the forbidden engine: he offered the stalled priests of Sofia esoteric scientific flattery and millions in research funding at the dinner table, while flanking them with a rotating harem of Inanna priestesses (models and masseuses). Like Honoré de Balzac’s master-criminal Vautrin (Trompe-la-Mort)—whom Girard analyzes as the subterranean Luciferian procurer who secretly rules the Parisian Kullaba elite by mediating their forbidden desires—Epstein became the supreme mediator precisely because his brazen, unpunished violation of the modern Kullaba’s ultimate taboo proved to his guests that he possessed sovereign, god-like autonomy:In Balzac's Illusions perdues and Splendeurs et misères des courtisanes, the escaped convict Vautrin (Jacques Collin) controls the upper echelons of the Parisian aristocracy, judiciary, and banking class by operating as a sexual procurer—grooming the courtesan Esther Gobseck to ensnare the billionaire banker Baron de Nucingen while maintaining an archive of blackmail letters that renders him untouchable by the law.

cit.quote: Epstein was not merely a financier; he was a collector of scientists, statesmen, and young women... To the academics who flew on his jets and attended his island conferences, he projected the intoxicating aura of a Renaissance prince [⁠Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta? ⁠Raimondo di Sangro? See section 8.3.3] who operated entirely above the petty bureaucratic rules and moral constraints of ordinary university life.
cit.bibl: Vicky Ward, The Talented Mr. Epstein, Vanity Fair (New York: Condé Nast, 2003), p. 158.

div.p: Crucially, this elite regression to the Sofia+Inanna BDMB is mirrored at the lower layers of the social pyramid by an identical mass-market turn toward badass worship. As we saw in Section 9.9, in impoverished urban neighborhoods where the traditional family and religious Kullaba have disintegrated, the Stage 1 civil-rights prophet of the 1960s has long since been replaced by Stage 3’s apex predator: the gangsta-rapper and the Drill music warlord. Dropping all pretense of political liberation, the contemporary street BDMB commands millions of streams—from both inner-city youth and middle-class suburban groupies—by explicitly broadcasting real-time murders of neighborhood rivals, flashing ostentatious luxury (tryphe), and parading a retinue of cosmetically armored baddies (the modern vernacular resurrection of the Sumerian kar-kid and the Azazel-taught courtesan of 1 Enoch). Linguistically, the triumph of the words badass (for male prestige) and baddie (for female aesthetic capital) marks the exact moment the postmodern E-Anna tore off the Kullaba glove: in Stage 3, the prefix Bad- is no longer ironic; it is an ontological requirement.

Even more revealing is how this mass-market craving for a demonic master has transformed the flagship genre of contemporary global cinema: the superhero and prestige-action narrative. In the immediate post-war era (Stage 1), popular cinema relied on lawful, Kullaba-aligned heroes who used violence strictly to defend the civic order. Today, because a polite, rule-abiding hero is despised by a Stage 3 audience as a boring, castrated Boy Scout, Hollywood screenwriters are forced to subject their cartoonish protagonists to a mandatory dark or villain turn. Whether it is the prestige-television canonization of unrepentant sociopaths (Tony Soprano, Walter White, Thomas Shelby, or the Gen Z internet idolization of the woman-murdering Wall Street banker Patrick Bateman as the ultimate Sigma Male) or the comic-book anti-hero who temporarily goes rogue and slaughters without mercy, the narrative mechanism is identical. By turning the hero into a temporary villain—or by making the villain the true, magnetic center of the film—the secular entertainment industry provides the audience with a safe, ticketed alibi to worship a Girardian bourreau délicieux (delightful executioner).Girard borrows the phrase bourreau délicieux from Charles Baudelaire to characterize the terminal masochistic stage of internal mediation, wherein the ontologically starved subject experiences the cruel, indifferent rival as a source of perverse, quasi-religious ecstasy; see René Girard, Deceit, Desire, and the Novel: Self and Other in Literary Structure, trans. Yvonne Freccero (Baltimore: Johns Hopkins Press, 1965), p. 181. For two hours in the dark theater, the domesticated modern citizen gets to thrill at the spectacle of a hyper-lethal Übermensch who tramples constitutional law underfoot, before the final five minutes hastily slip the Kullaba glove back on to satisfy moral censorship.

And when we examine the internal architecture of these blockbuster superhero franchises—most notably in iconic archetypes like Tony Stark (Iron Man) or Bruce Wayne (Batman)—we discover the exact same Frederician Sofia plus Inanna blueprint that animated Jeffrey Epstein’s island and Keith Raniere’s compound. The modern cinematic demigod is almost invariably a billionaire technocrat who possesses miraculous, quasi-magical scientific gnosis (Sofia), which he uses to forge an invincible suit of armor or an arsenal of futuristic weapons, while simultaneously operating as a playboy BDMB surrounded by supermodels and lethal, skin-tight-leather-clad femmes fatales (Inanna). From the private jets winging Nobel physicists and fashion models to Little Saint James, down to the multiplex screen where millions of teenagers worship a billionaire vigilante flanked by an AI goddess and a martial-erotic heroine, postmodern Western culture is running a single, monolithic religious program: the desperate attempt to resurrect the ancient E-Anna sovereign by fusing technocratic gnosis with the transgressive aura of the executioner. This is the New Religious Movement we talked about in Chapter 1. It is now the West's dominant religion.

div.head: 10.4 The Latest Bourreau Délicieux — Israel-Bashing as the New Covert Monster-Worship
div.p: Once we recognize that the sado-masochistic worship of the demonic BDMB is the dominant, unacknowledged religion of the contemporary West, one of the most baffling geopolitical phenomena of our time suddenly snaps into focus: the all-consuming, quasi-religious obsession with the State of Israel among the European and American coastal elites and their middle-class progressive groupies. In an August 26, 2026 appearance on The Brink podcast, the historian Simon Sebag Montefiore aptly diagnosed this collective frenzy, observing that in the contemporary Western ideological landscape, hating Israel is the new religion:

cit.quote: Hating Israel has become the new religion of the Western elite... The two-state solution has become a theological dogma, and the denunciation of the Jewish state now functions as the primary liturgy through which progressive Westerners—who are otherwise busy demolishing the history and religious foundations of their own countries—signal their moral salvation.
cit.bibl: Simon Sebag Montefiore, interview by Jake Wallis Simons and Andrew Fox, Hating Israel Is The New Religion, The Brink podcast (August 26, 2026).

div.p: While Montefiore’s empirical observation is spot-on, our Girardian and Kullaba-E-Anna framework allows us to go a step further: Israel-hating is not a separate new religion; it is merely the latest geopolitical avatar of the exact same Stage 3 monster-worship we have been tracing throughout this chapter. The primary question regarding the Western fixation on Israel is one of glaring thermodynamic disproportion: why does a localized territorial conflict in the Levant generate an ecstatic, round-the-clock liturgical frenzy on Ivy League campuses and in European ministries, while far deadlier wars and actual genocides across the globe elicit total indifference? The answer lies in the geometry of the black. As we saw in Sections 3.2 and 9.10, when a culture operating under strict egalitarian taboos is forbidden from openly worshipping a master in the red, its starved metaphysical desire can only express itself invertedly—as hatred, or what we diagnosed in the feminist pornoprophetic critics (Section 9.9) as confession-through-projection.

For the ontologically castrated Western Kullaba clerk, the fantasized image of the hyper-efficient, ultra-cruel IDF soldier ruthlessly machine-gunning babies in Gaza functions as the ultimate collective bourreau délicieux—the geopolitical Nikolai Stavrogin of our day. Consider the structural position of post-WWII Western Europe and its ideological twin in the US coastal bureaucracy: having outsourced its Second Function (bellatores) for eighty years and locked itself inside Max Weber’s bureaucratic iron cage, the Western ruling class governs exclusively through international tribunals, UN resolutions, NGOs, and human-rights lecturing—the secularized remnants of the priesthood’s linguistic prestige. Yet, deep down, this demilitarized Kullaba elite is disgusted by its own impotence. When Israel—a culturally familiar, Westernized, democratic nation—suddenly shrugs off the International Criminal Court, ignores the moral scolding of European capitals, and wages kinetic, existential warfare with brazen indifference to liberal disapproval, it acts exactly like Sargon of Akkad (Section 5.2.2) or Frederick II (Section 8.3.1) defying the priestly Kullaba. Because the progressive academic or middle-class activist cannot openly admire raw martial sovereignty in the red, they indulge their fascination negatively: by endlessly conjuring, sharing, and embellishing demonic mental images of a remorseless Zionist Übermensch trampling every humanitarian taboo, they get to stare into the forbidden sun of the E-Anna under the virtuous alibi of moral horror:

cit.quote: This is the passion we call hatred... The subject is convinced that the model’s indifference toward him is the sign of a supreme, self-sufficient divinity. The more the model spurns our laws and our protests, the more we secretly suspect that he alone possesses the secret of being, and our moral indignation is merely the mask worn by our frustrated adoration.
cit.bibl: René Girard, Deceit, Desire, and the Novel: Self and Other in Literary Structure, trans. Yvonne Freccero (Baltimore: Johns Hopkins Press, 1965), pp. 41, 179.

div.p: What renders the Israeli avatar utterly irresistible to the subconscious of the postmodern West, however, is that it does not merely project raw military force; it projects the complete, archaic Sofia plus Inanna synthesis in its native Levantine habitat. On the Sofia side, Israel is globally perceived as the supreme Start-Up Nation—the land of cyber-warfare, AI targeting systems, exploding pagers, and the quasi-magical, impenetrable shield of the Iron Dome. Just like the superhero’s futuristic armor or Epstein’s transhumanist salon, Israel’s technological supremacy represents the pinnacle of mathematical, demiurgic gnosis weaponized for survival. To the stalled academic priesthoods of the West, the Israeli military-technological complex is a rogue Sofia engine that refuses to stay inside the polite but sterile, peer-reviewed boundaries of the university.

Even more potently, on the Inanna side, this high-tech Sofia shield is paired in the global digital bloodstream with an overt, state-sponsored martial-erotic iconography that has no equivalent anywhere else in the modern world: the viral phenomenon of female IDF conscripts on TikTok and Instagram. In tens of thousands of short videos that have garnered hundreds of millions of views worldwide, heavily made-up, strikingly attractive eighteen- and nineteen-year-old Israeli women—clad in tight olive-drab uniforms, combat helmets, and tactical vests, with M16 or Tavor assault rifles slung across their hips and Merkava main battle tanks rumbling in the desert background—dance provocatively to Manu Chao’s Me Gustas Tú (I Like You) or techno beats right on the edge of the Gaza battlefield. Visually, anthropologically, and geographically, this is a near-perfect, verbatim re-enactment of ancient Levantine Astarte (Inanna-Ishtar) worship from three thousand years ago—the armed, seductive kar-kid priestesses performing the ešen (play/dance of love and lethal combat, Section 9.9) before the warband. While the Western progressive consciously denounces these videos as war-crime propaganda, their reptilian brain is completely mesmerized by the spectacle.

div.head: 10.5 Epilogue — The Campus by Day and by Night
div.p: We have come full circle, returning to the exact institutional setting where our investigation began in Chapter 1: the elite American university campus. As we documented at the outset, contemporary Western youth are suffering from an unprecedented psychological and relational collapse—skyrocketing suicide rates, a massive surge in antidepressant and anxiolytic dependency, and a profound sex recession that has left a deeply alienated generation starving for ontological weight. Yet, rather than offering an exit from this existential desert, the elite Ivy League campus (Cornell, Columbia, Harvard, Yale) functions as the supreme cathedral of the West’s unacknowledged Stage 3 religion. Stripped of the protective armor of Christian porneiomachia and trapped inside the ruthless, competitive panopticon of the black, the university student body is caught in a permanent oscillation between two complementary liturgies of sado-masochistic BDMB worship—one performed in the sunlight of the campus quad, the other in the clandestine shadows of the fraternity house.

By day, the campus operates under the virtuous, pseudo-Kullaba catechism of intersectional critical theory and FCNSW (Section 9.10). Here, the students and their faculty mentors congregate in protest encampments, simultaneously indulging both halves of their Girardian pathology. On the one hand, re-enacting the 1970s Radical Chic nostalgie de la boue diagnosed by Tom Wolfe, the polite, upper-middle-class students deck themselves in keffiyehs and chant slogans alongside masked militants, vicariously huffing the raw, patriarchal, martial-erotic fumes of an archaic Männerbund under the progressive alibi of championing resistance. On the other hand, they whip themselves into an ecstatic, voyeuristic frenzy of moral horror over their collective bourreau délicieux: the phantom of the high-tech, Astarte-flanked Israeli super-soldier. Forbidden by their egalitarian dogma from openly worshipping a sovereign master in the red, the daytime campus liturgy allows them to stare endlessly at the forbidden sun of unmediated martial-erotic power through the inverted lens of demonic hatred.

Then night falls, and the ideological alibis of the quad dissolve into the physical praxis of the McThelema sanctuary. By night, the alienated female student—the sorority Stacy or our Cornell Jane Doe—walks across the dark campus into the Chi Phi fraternity house to physically submit to the local Chad BDMB and his kóryos brotherhood. Offering her body as a drug tray and group-sex vessel in an orgiastic act of reputational suicide, she enacts in the flesh the exact same terminal sacrament that her peers perform ideologically on the quad, that her professors theorize in their seminars, and that the global ruling class consummated on Jeffrey Epstein’s island. Six thousand years after the first mud-brick precincts were raised in Late Chalcolithic Uruk, the protective glove of the Kullaba lies in shreds, and the Western world kneels once more—naked, intoxicated, and begging for transfiguration—before the unmasked altar of the E-Anna.
